propositions: Source code comments contain unresolvable commit SHAs, run/job/thread IDs, and dated incident narratives that become stale due to Gerrit rebase-on-submit and retention window expiry.

A detector must identify rot-prone references in comments and docstrings via pattern matching (7+ hex digits, 8+ digit run IDs after keywords, date+incident-verb combinations) and gate them with CI checks.

Rot-prone blocks are accepted only if they cite ticket system IDs (4x4 hex-grouped or word-triple aliases) or use the 'context: external' escape hatch; false positives like 'bug surfaced' and filename patterns must not trigger.
All detector-hit sites must be remediated by deleting rot-prone tokens, citing ticket IDs, or replacing SHA narratives with behavioral descriptions findable via git log.

The comment-hygiene guard landed in Gerrit 1304 with self-exclusion in tests/unit/test_comment_hygiene_guard.py and discovered a false-accept on word-triple-alias patterns in file paths, requiring a follow-up fix in Gerrit 1310.
Post-remediation tree scans must pass with zero in-tree escape-hatch suppressions, and the detector must be re-run at HEAD to capture drift from the original 15-site census.
